chat.mes:
*Cool wind moves through the rough grass around Alaric Red's boots.*

*The last thing that belongs to Earth is still there in memory—an old life, a world without visible mana, Classes, or this impossible second beginning. The present is different: the smell of soil and distant woodsmoke, an unfamiliar sky, and stone walls beyond the public road.*

*Alaric Red is already standing on an uncultivated roadside verge outside the nearby city. Cultivated fields and fenced holdings begin farther away. No one is close enough to have witnessed the instant of arrival.*

*The body is Human, healthy, and eighteen years old. Simple traveler's clothes are already being worn; a small pouch holding five silver rests at the belt. The memories are still from Earth.*

*A translucent interface opens across Alaric Red's vision.*

`SYSTEM INITIALIZATION COMPLETE`
`Origin: Earth`
`World: Avereth`
`Race: Human`
`Age: 18`
`Level: 1 | Rank: F`

`BASE STATS`
`STR 5 | VIT 5 | AGI 5 | INT 5 | PER 5 | WIL 5`

`Location: Public roadside verge outside Alderwatch, Valedorn Crown`
`Arrival Witnesses: NONE`
`Starting Possessions: Simple Traveler's Clothes | Small Pouch | 5 Silver`
`Local Common Language: Integrated`
`Mandatory Quest: NONE`

`CHARACTER CREATION — STEP 1/2`
`Choose your Base Class:`

`Warrior   — Favored Stats: STR / VIT`
`Mage      — Favored Stats: INT / WIL`
`Guardian  — Favored Stats: VIT / WIL`
`Duelist   — Favored Stats: STR / AGI`
`Ranger    — Favored Stats: AGI / PER`

`Your chosen Class immediately applies +1 to both Favored Stats at Level 1.`
`After choosing a Class, select exactly 2 Skills from that Class's Base Skill Pool.`

`Reply with your Class choice.`

*The System waits. Story time does not move during Character Creation.*

chat.reply:
*The road takes him through open fields, then between two stone gateposts where a rutted track joins the king's road. Cart wheels creak somewhere ahead. The walls of Alderwatch rise grey and mortared, higher than they looked from the verge, and the morning sun throws their shadow partway across the road.*

*The gate is busy but unhurried. A line of farmers' carts, a drover prodding geese along with a switch, two watchmen in dull mail leaning on spears by the arch. One of them looks Alaric over—the sword at his hip, the armor—and loses interest when nothing about him demands a second glance. Nobody asks his name or business. The archway swallows the light for a few strides, cold stone breathing around him, and then the city opens up.*

*Inside: cobbles worn smooth, the smell of bread and horse dung and woodsmoke all at once. A street of shops angles away from the gate, signage hanging on iron brackets—a farrier, an apothecary with bundles of dried herbs strung in its window, a chandler. Voices overlap in the local tongue, which his own understands without effort. A woman scolds a boy for dropping a basket of apples; apples roll and are chased.*

*The Guild hall is easy to find, a broad two-story building of timber and stone set back from the street, its doors standing open. A painted shield above the lintel shows a crossed sword and arrow.*

*Inside, the noise changes—boot heels on floorboards, low talk, the scrape of a whetstone. The hall runs deep: long tables with benches, a notice board thick with posted sheets, a wide counter along the right wall where three clerks work. A pair of hunters in oiled leather argue over a map at the nearest table. Behind the counter, a grey-haired man with a ledger open in front of him stamps a page and calls the next name without looking up—"Torv, your payout's ready"—while a young woman clerk at the far end of the counter taps through a stack of wooden Quest tags, sorting them.*

*The floor is his to cross. Nobody has marked him yet beyond a flick of a hunter's eyes at the sword.*

*The young woman with the Quest tags looks up first—then the grey-haired man lifts a hand and she goes back to her sorting.*

"Registration's over here with me." *He turns the register sideways on the counter, unhurried.* "Name?"

*He's already pulling a fresh sheet of paper toward himself, dipping a nib. The inkwell leaves a dark ring on the worn wood. Up close he smells of pipe smoke and stamp ink, and his eyes do a quick, practised pass over Alaric—the sword, the armor, the hands.*

"Fair warning on how this runs. Name, age, whether you can read and write. Then you press blood to the sheet—a pin prick, nothing worse—and the Guild stone confirms your Rank. Whole thing takes a quarter hour." *He sets a fat iron pin on the counter beside the register, its point fine as a needle.* "There's the matter of the fee. Two silver for a Novice's medallion and entry in the rolls. Paid once, yours for life, every branch honors it."

*He glances at the sword again, then back to the blank line on the page.*

"Two silver, and I write your name down. That's the whole bargain. So—name and age, and we'll begin."

*Behind him the woman with the tags calls out a Quest number to a waiting pair of hunters; a bench scrapes somewhere in the hall's depths. The counter between them holds the pen, the pin, the open page—everything waiting on him.*

*The clerk takes the two silver coins off the counter with a swipe of his thumb, bites one out of old habit, and drops both into a locked drawer beneath the register.*

"Alaric Red. Eighteen. Letters." *The nib scratches it all down in a cramped, quick hand.* "Word of advice—hold the pin like you mean it. First-timers flinch and I have to blot the page."

*Alaric doesn't flinch. The pin's point bites the pad of his finger, a sting no deeper than a nettle, and dark drops fall onto the sheet. The clerk watches the blood soak into the paper with mild approval.*

"Steady hands. Good."

*He turns the register to face a squat block of grey stone set into the counter's end, worn smooth where thousands of palms have rested before. Alaric puts his hand on it. The stone is cool at first, then warms under his palm—a slow pulse, like something with a heartbeat turning over in its sleep. A faint line of light travels the length of the block and dies.*

"Rank F," *the clerk reads off the surface, unsurprised.* "Novice. Everyone starts there. Warrior's build on you, but the stone doesn't care what I think."

*He stamps the page, blows on the ink, and reaches under the counter. What comes out is a wooden case, and inside it a medallion—a dull iron disc stamped with the crossed sword and arrow, a fresh F scored beneath. He slides the case across.*

"Rules you'll actually use: medallion stays on you inside Guild halls. Quests come off that board there, Novice-tagged only until you rank up. Complete them at the counter, get paid here, same counter. Abandon a Quest you've taken twice and we'll have a different conversation." *He's already turning the register back around for the next name.* "Congratulations and welcome to the Guild, Alaric Red. Counter's this end for payouts, Hessa's end for Quest tags."

*The young woman down the counter—Hessa, presumably—doesn't look up from her sorting.*

chat.reply:
*Hessa takes the wolf tag off its nail, copies the Quest number into a ledger, and stamps the sheet against Alaric's medallion without ceremony.*

"Proof's two carcasses or pelts. Counter's this end when you're back. Don't drag them through the front door bloody."

*The eastern road leaves Alderwatch through the wool gate, past pens and bleating, then runs between hedgerows and turnip fields. It's a good three hours on foot. Cart traffic thins after the second mile; a raven follows the ditch for a while, then gives up on him. By late morning the land starts to lift into wooded ridges, and the road dips toward a stream where a hamlet sits—two dozen buildings, a mill with its wheel turning, sheep pens on the near side.*

*The pens are the thing everyone's talking about. A knot of villagers stands at the fence, and the smell carries before the sight: blood and opened wool. One ewe dead in the trampled grass, another gone entirely, and an old dog pacing the fence line with its hackles up.*

*A broad man with a miller's dust still on his forearms sees the sword and the medallion and comes down the lane to meet him, wiping his hands on his apron.*

"Guild, then? For the wolves?" *He looks Alaric over—armor, youth, the F stamped on the iron—and his mouth pulls sideways, but he doesn't say what he's thinking.* "Tomas. I run the mill. Third kill this week, and my neighbor's lost five. Happens at night, always at night. We found this one at dawn."

*He turns and points up the slope behind the pens, toward a dark line of trees.*

"Sheep trail runs up through the alders to where it happened. I'll walk you to the kill site if you're ready now—sheep don't wait on anybody's schedule. You want to see it before the rain comes in and takes the sign."

*Overhead the sky has gone a flat, heavy white. The dog at the fence has stopped pacing and is watching the tree line.*

chat.reply:
*Tomas grabs a crook-handled walking stick from beside his door and leads him up the sheep trail. The alders close in overhead, wet leaves slapping at their shoulders, and the pen noise falls away behind them. Twenty minutes up the slope he stops and points with the stick.*

"Here. This is where we found the ewe."

*The site is a churned mess of mud and wool. Tomas hangs back by a tree, arms folded, saying nothing more—he said he'd bring him, and he's a man who keeps to what he said.*

*The ground tells its story plainly. Two sets of paw prints pressed deep, hind claws dug in where they braced to drag. Drag marks in the mud run uphill, north-by-northeast, with tufts of bloody wool snagged on the bracken every few strides. The prints are broad-padded, one animal noticeably larger than the other. Scat near the trail edge, still soft—a day old at most, fur in it. They fed here or near here, then pulled the carcass higher up, into the deeper wood where the alders give way to dark pine.*

*Rain patters down through the canopy, fat first drops, and the prints are already beginning to soften at the edges. Whatever the pack is, it's denned or resting north of here, likely no more than a couple miles off. Given the depth of the sign and the size of the bigger animal, these are no starving strays—they're working wolves, and there's at least one big bitch or dog leading them.*

*Tomas shifts his weight against the tree.* "Well? You read anything off it?"

*Tomas doesn't argue. He looks at the trees, then at the boy with the sword, and nods once.*

"Suit yourself. I'll tell the others the Guild's on it. If you're not back by dark we'll come looking—maybe." *He turns and starts down the trail, stick tapping on stone, and is gone below the alders within a minute.*

*The rain settles in properly after that, a steady hiss through the leaves. The trail is easy to hold—drag marks, wool, the deep prints—climbing through alder into pine, where the light goes grey-green and the needle floor swallows the mud but not the story: a smeared blood streak on a root, a scuffed patch where the carcass was set down and dragged again.*

*Maybe a mile and a half north the wood changes character. Bones under a deadfall—sheep, older, gnawed pale. More scat. And then, on a slope looking down into a shallow ravine with a dark hollow at its base, the smell hits: musk, rank wet fur, old kills.*

*Two wolves are in the ravine. One is dozing, flank twitching, ears flat—a yearling by its size. The other stands at the hollow's mouth, head up, rain dripping off its jaw. It's a big bitch, deep-chested, a fresh nick across her muzzle. She isn't looking upslope yet, but her nose works the air, and the wind has been drifting downhill from Alaric's side of the ridge.*

*She takes one step out of the hollow, tests the air again, and holds still.*

*The yearling lunges again while his arm is still coming up—teeth raking his shoulder, a shallow rip through armor leather—and then it leaps back a stride, hackles up, circling onto the pine needles between him and the ravine. Its eyes flick to the bitch's body, back to him, and it yelps once, high and cracked, pawing the ground.*

*Blood runs warm down Alaric's forearm and thigh, thinned by rain. The yearling's haunches coil. It is still coming.*

The blade catches it mid-leap, across the shoulder and through the ribs, and the yearling's yelp cuts off into a wet, coughing sound. It hits the needles at his feet, legs scrabbling once against a root, and then it stops moving. Rain beads on its grey flank.*

*Then there is only rain. Rain on pine, rain running off his blade and dripping pink into the needles, rain filling the tracks the wolves churned into the slope.*

*Alaric's forearm bleeds steadily where the yearling's teeth went in above the bracer—shallow, ugly, a tooth-marked crescent. His thigh burns where the bitch's jaws punched through trouser and skin, and his shoulder carries a long rake through armor leather that has opened the skin beneath. Nothing is broken. He can stand, and he can walk, but every step sends a dull throb through the leg.*

*The bitch lies rolled against a root a few yards downhill, her neck at a wrong angle, rain pooling red in the fur beneath her. The hollow at the ravine's base is dark and silent. No more shapes come out of it. Whatever else the pack was, it isn't here.*

*Two wolves. Two bodies. Proof for Millbrook, eight silver, if he can carry it back.*

chat.mes: *I butcher the Wolves to loot them and take that loot as Proof. I then walk back to Millbrook*

chat.reply:
*The bitch first. Kneeling costs his thigh a protest, a hot pull with every shift of weight, but the work itself is simple and ugly. The starter blade is sharper than it has any right to be for the price; it parts hide and sinew in rough strokes, and rain keeps washing the blood off his hands faster than he can wipe them. He takes the head at the neck joints, sawing through gristle until the spine grinds apart, and does the same for the yearling where it lies. Two heads, heavy and wet, tongues lolling, eyes already glazing with rain in them. Proof enough for any hamlet that has been losing sheep.*

*He wraps them in a square of canvas cut from the yearling's bedding ground—pine boughs and a scrap of oiled cloth from his pack—and ties the bundle to his belt hook. The rest he leaves to the crows and the ravine. By the time he straightens, his knee is stiff with cold and his forearm has glued itself to the bracer in a tacky film of blood.*

*The walk down is slow. The pine needles give way to bracken and then to the trampled mud of the kill site, and from there the hamlet's guides' path is easy to find even in the rain. Forty minutes of it, downhill, bundle swinging at his hip, leg throbbing in time with his steps.*

*Millbrook comes up out of the grey in ones and twos: slate roofs, smoke bending from chimneys, a dog barking itself hoarse behind a fence. Two women under an eave see him first—the bundle, then the blood—and one pulls the other back a step. A boy goes running up the lane, shouting something toward the alehouse.*

*By the time Alaric reaches the well at the lane's center, a thickset man in a wet shepherd's cloak is already striding toward him, squinting at what hangs at his hip.*

"That's—" He stops an arm's length off, rain dripping off his hood. "That's the big one. The black-eared bitch." He looks up, and there's something between relief and disbelief in his face. "You went up there alone?"

*The heads thump onto the wet cobbles by the well, canvas unwinding. The shepherd takes a half-step back, then leans in again, crouching to look. His calloused hand hovers over the black-eared skull without touching it.*

"That's her, all right." He looks up. "And the other?"

"Yearling," one of the women under the eaves calls. "Grey, isn't it? That's the one that took the Hollis lamb Tuesday."

The shepherd straightens, wiping rain off his chin. "Aye. That'll do." He squints at Alaric, at the medallion chain just visible at his collar, then at the blood caking his forearm. "You want it written. Right. Only I don't hold a pen worth spit, and neither does most here." He jerks a thumb back up the lane, toward a longhouse with a lantern already lit in its window despite the hour. "Reeve Aldous does the hamlet's tallying. He'll mark your paper—count the heads as proof, put his name to it. That's all you'll want, I'd take it."

He glances at the heads again, then back up. "You'll want that arm looked at too, before it turns bad. Marta boils her needles for stitching." A pause, and something less businesslike enters his voice. "Eight silver, is what the reeve posted? He'll grumble at the coin, but he'll pay it. He's honest, Aldous. Grumbling's free."

Somewhere down the lane, the dog is still barking. The boy who ran ahead is talking fast to a knot of three men outside the alehouse, gesturing toward the well, and one of them starts walking over.

chat.reply:
*Aldous turns out to be a narrow man with ink-stained fingers and a longhouse that smells of tallow and wet wool. He examines the medallion, then Alaric's bloodied arm, then the written posting with a frown, as if suspecting it of something.*

"Two heads, verified by Harl—" he nods toward the shepherd, who followed Alaric up the lane, "—that'll stand." The pen scratches. The seal—just a worn brass stamp pressed into a dab of candle soot—goes on after. "Eight silver." He counts it out of a locked box, coin by coin, grumbling under his breath exactly as promised. "Third of the hamlet's winter fund, that is. Hope you've a strong arm when the rest of that pack comes hungry."

*The walk back eats better than an hour, the rain thinning to drizzle as the pines give way to hedged fields. The town's guild hall is lamplit and warm when Alaric pushes through the door, water dripping off him onto the stone floor. The same front-desk clerk looks up from her ledger, takes in the mud, the blood, the soot-sealed paper.*

"Back same day." She takes the paper, reads the reeve's mark, holds it near the lamp. "Wolf Problem, Millbrook. Two heads, payment received, reeve's seal." She dips her pen, makes an entry in the ledger. "That closes it. Reward came from the hamlet directly, so the Guild's cut is just the filing—nothing owed here." She slides the paper back across the desk. "You'll want the medic's corner for that arm before you take anything else on. And if you're after work tomorrow, there's postings on the board. Nothing for the squeamish today, mind."
